one_line: Governments tighten AI rules, OpenAI boosts safety, compute expands, and drug‑AI funding surges.

themes.title: Governments reshape AI policy
themes.text: Swedish government ministries banned staff from using ChatGPT and Claude, requiring Microsoft Copilot. The UK will spend £100 million on a national AI Biosecurity Lab, India will issue an AI law consultation paper, and Poland’s prime minister called for deeper AI, digital and space cooperation with India.

stories.headline: Swedish government offices ban ChatGPT and Claude, require Microsoft Copilot
UK to invest £100 million in AI Biosecurity Lab
India to issue AI law consultation paper in coming weeks, says minister
Polish prime minister calls for deeper AI, digital and space cooperation with India

themes.title: OpenAI enhances safety protocols
themes.text: OpenAI resumed training its most advanced models in an offline environment and added offline containment and high‑compute red‑team checks. The company also terminated three safety researchers after an internal investigation alleged they leaked internal model designs.

stories.headline: OpenAI trains frontier AI models without internet access
OpenAI details new containment measures for frontier model training
OpenAI fires three safety researchers over alleged leak of internal model designs

themes.title: AI compute infrastructure scales up
themes.text: OpenAI made its Decisions API generally available with voice and visual inputs, pricing $0.10 per million input tokens. SpaceX plans to manage 13 GW of AI compute capacity by the end of 2027. OpenAI upgraded its Habitat storage system to deliver reads twelve times faster for ChatGPT users.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Decisions API with voice, visual inputs at $0.10 per million tokens
SpaceX aims for 13 GW AI compute capacity by end of 2027
OpenAI scales Habitat storage to deliver 12× faster reads for ChatGPT

themes.title: Funding fuels AI drug discovery
themes.text: Warp Sciences raised $215 million to build AI‑powered chemistry labs for drug research. Pathos AI secured a $237 million Series E round at a $3 billion valuation and partnered with Bristol Myers Squibb and Tempus AI to accelerate Alzheimer’s drug development.

stories.headline: Warp Sciences raises $215 million to build AI‑powered drug research labs
Pathos AI raises $237 million Series E led by Bristol Myers Squibb
Pathos AI partners with Bristol Myers Squibb and Tempus AI on Alzheimer drug development
